questions.question: A dependency loses support in ten weeks and migration is estimated at three to five weeks. A PM opens a document on the team's long-term dependency-risk policy. What is the strongest objection?
options: Policy work belongs to engineering leadership, not to product
The document is fine, but it should be timeboxed to one week
The next consequential choice — migrate in one block or spread the work — can be made without it, so the document delays the decision while resembling diligence
Ten weeks is too short a horizon to reason about policy usefully
questions.explanation: This is the removal test. Delete the broadest section and ask whether the next choice can still be made; here it can, so the section is context rather than framing. B is the tempting distractor: timeboxing limits the cost of the wrong-sized frame without fixing the size, and the week still comes out of a ten-week window.

questions.question: Which choice most clearly justifies a broad frame?
options: A one-way choice whose consequence is large and which will set the precedent later decisions follow
A high-consequence choice that can be reversed within a sprint at low cost
A low-consequence choice that is expensive to reverse
A choice several senior stakeholders hold strong and conflicting opinions about
questions.explanation: Only high consequence combined with one-way commitment justifies broad framing, and precedent-setting widens it further. D is the tempting distractor because stakeholder heat feels like a reason to frame broadly, but disagreement is a fact about the room, not a property of the choice — a broad frame there usually buys consensus theatre rather than a better decision.

questions.question: A PM narrows the dependency question to "which two engineers take the migration." What is the specific defect?
options: Staffing questions should always follow scoping questions in sequence
It excludes the timing choice, so the consequence of a wrong answer — running past end-of-support — lands outside the frame
It ignores the possibility of hiring a contractor for the migration
Two engineers is too few for a three-to-five-week estimate with wide uncertainty
questions.explanation: A frame must be at least large enough to contain the consequence of getting the answer wrong. Staffing cannot absorb a timing failure. D is tempting because it engages with the estimate, but it argues about the answer inside the narrow frame rather than noticing that the frame excludes the real risk.

questions.question: The case notes that after end-of-support, security patches stop but nothing breaks immediately. How does this fact bear on frame size?
options: It lowers consequence, so the choice can be deferred until something visibly breaks
It raises consequence, because unpatched software is an immediate outage risk
It is background context and does not affect framing
It separates the axes: nothing breaking keeps near-term disruption low, while patches stopping makes the exposure accumulate and hard to reverse — so the frame must cover timing, not just execution
questions.explanation: Consequence and reversibility must be judged separately, and this fact points in different directions on each. A is the tempting distractor and the most common real-world reading: it collapses both axes into "not urgent", which is precisely how a ten-week window becomes a six-week one.

questions.question: A narrow frame produced an answer the PM dislikes, so they widen the frame and re-run the analysis. When is this legitimate?
options: Whenever the first answer conflicts with the PM's judgment, since judgment is what a PM is for
When new evidence or a newly visible consequence changed what the frame must contain — and the widening is stated openly, along with what it changes
Never; a frame committed to at the start of the work cannot be revised
When a more senior stakeholder requests a broader view
questions.explanation: Frames are judgments under incomplete information and can be revised, but the trigger must be a change in the world rather than a change in how much you like the answer. A is the tempting distractor because PM judgment is real; the difference is that legitimate re-framing is declared before the outcome is known, not applied afterwards to find a scale at which you win.
